title: Cohort-adaptive thresholds and rollback SLA matrix for Optimize evals
creator: Anika Rao
description: Product requirements for introducing cohort-adaptive evaluation thresholds and a per-cohort SLA/rollback matrix in Optimize. The goal is to make A/B and canary gating sensitive to user segmentation and prompt-set variability while reducing noisy false positives and enabling controlled human overrides for borderline regressions.
problem_statement: Current Optimize evals use global, fixed regression thresholds and single aggregated signals which either cause unnecessary rollbacks on small noisy slices or miss regressions that affect specific customer cohorts. We need a specification for prompt-set partitioning, cohort-aware thresholds, composite signal calculation, and human-in-the-loop fuzzy rollback rules.
objective: Deliver a repeatable, auditable gating system that: 1) computes per-cohort baselines and adaptive thresholds; 2) exposes composite quality signals for routing in the Console; 3) defines deterministic A/B pass/fail rules and a fuzzy rollback flow for ambiguous cases.
scope_in: Define cohort partitioning heuristics (traffic-based, enterprise vs self-serve, verticals)
Specify prompt-set slicing for each cohort and minimum sample requirements
Design composite signal (accuracy, toxicity proxy, response-length drift, embedding-similarity) with weights
Acceptance criteria and numerical thresholds for canary and A/B gates
Rollback playbook including human review steps and override UI hooks
scope_out: Full model retraining or dataset creation processes
Billing or pricing changes for customers
Deep privacy analysis for cohort definitions (handled by Security separately)
promptset_sampling: Per-cohort stratified sampling: ensure minimum 1k queries or 7-day window whichever is larger
Sample by intent cluster (>=3 intent buckets per cohort) to avoid domination by a single prompt
Include a fixed control prompt subset (50 prompts) used across all cohorts for anchor comparisons
Refresh sampling weekly; maintain historical snapshots for backfill comparisons
metrics: composite_quality_score: weighted mean of quality signals (weights configurable per cohort)
delta_absolute: absolute change in composite_quality_score vs cohort baseline
directional_regression_rate: percent of prompts with worse label/score >= threshold
embedding_drift: mean cosine drop vs baseline control subset
safety_signal_rate: fraction of responses flagged by automated safety proxies
baseline: Baseline computed as the 28-day rolling median per cohort. For new cohorts (age <14 days) use platform-wide baseline with conservative threshold scaling.
acceptance_criteria: Per-cohort composite_quality_score must not degrade by more than 2.5 percentage points (absolute) with p<0.01 over two consecutive windows (each window = 24 hours of traffic or min sample) to pass canary
A/B criteria: treatment must show non-inferior composite_quality_score within delta=1.5 points with 95% confidence for high-priority cohorts and delta=3.0 for low-priority cohorts
Minimum sample: each A/B cell must have >= 1k evaluated responses or test is inconclusive
No cohort may exhibit safety_signal_rate increase >0.2 percentage points absolute without an approved mitigation plan
If embedding_drift > 0.05 (mean cosine drop) on control subset, block rollout until root cause analysis is completed
rollout_plan: Step 0: Local dev tests and synthetic prompt-set evals (automated)
Step 1: Internal canary (10% internal traffic routing, 72h) — immediate automated gating against acceptance_criteria
Step 2: Tiered customer canary: start with non-critical cohorts (5% of public traffic) for 48h, then expand to 25% if signals stable
Step 3: Platform-wide gradual ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 24h stabilization windows and automated checks at each milestone
Human-in-the-loop: if a borderline case is detected, page SRE/PM and open a review in Console with comparison dashboards and suggested rollback severity
rollback_triggers: Hard trigger: any cohort shows delta_absolute >= 5 points and p<0.001 over a single 24h window -> automatic emergency rollback
Soft trigger: cohort delta between 2.5 and 5 points OR safety_signal_rate increase between 0.05 and 0.2 -> pause rollout and create incident with mandatory human review within 2 hours

Fuzzy trigger: small degradations (1.5-2.5 points) combined with increased variance or customer complaints will surface in Console as 'requires review' and allow a manual rollback or staged mitigation
Cohort-specific SLA breach: if an enterprise cohort's composite_quality_score drops below contractual SLA for >6 hours, initiate escalation to Account Team and consider prioritized rollback
monitoring_signals: Per-prompt regression heatmap and top-k failing prompts
Customer-reported incidents tied to cohort tags
Model inference latency and token-error rate (to disambiguate infra issues)
Post-deployment AB lift charts and Bayesian posterior probability of regression
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Use per-cohort thresholds to reduce false positives at the cost of more complex configuration and operational overhead
Conservative default weights for composite signals to prioritize safety and perceived correctness
Adopt fuzzy rollback to avoid oscillation from noisy short-term signals — requires human review UI investments
Reject global fixed thresholds: unacceptable for customers with highly skewed prompt distributions
